snip.t: Hyponatraemia: Excess free water intake, SIADH, heart failure, liver cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, thiazide diuretics, adrenal insufficiency — Severe malaria (SIADH), TB meningitis (SIADH), HIV‑associated adrenal disease, chronic diarrhoea from dysentery

Hypocalcaemia: Vitamin D deficiency, hypoparathyroidism, renal failure, acute pancreatitis, massive transfusion — HIV‑related malabsorption, TB meningitis (calcitonin dysregulation), chronic diarrhoea, malaria‑induced hypomagnesaemia
Gastro‑intestinal: Acute gastroenteritis, chronic diarrhoea (e.g., from parasitic infection) — Direct fluid loss, electrolyte depletion

qs.q: A 40-year-old female presents with chronic diarrhoea, weight loss, and abdominal pain. Biopsy of the small intestine shows villous atrophy and intraepithelial lymphocytosis. She is positive for anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) antibodies. What is the diagnosis?
qs.e: Chronic diarrhoea, weight loss, villous atrophy, increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, and positive anti-tTG antibodies are diagnostic of celiac disease.

qs.q: A 50-year-old male presents with a history of chronic diarrhoea, weight loss, and abdominal pain. Small bowel biopsy shows villous atrophy, increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, and positive anti-tTG antibodies. What is the most appropriate long-term management?
qs.e: The diagnosis of celiac disease, confirmed by biopsy and serology, requires a lifelong gluten-free diet to manage symptoms and prevent complications.
